title: Doers of the Word
subtitle: James in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
James is a short letter of plain wisdom: trials and endurance, the rich and the poor, faith that works, a tongue that sets forests on fire, and a farmer waiting for rain.

This book walks through its five chapters in thirty short poems. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture, so you can read it in an evening, or one page a morning.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the letter of James alongside this one, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: the kiln
paintings.epigraph: “the testing of your faith produces endurance.”
paintings.poem:
count it joy, he says—
not the trial,
but what the trial is making.

clay doesn't enjoy the kiln.
but it comes out
able to hold water.

endurance is not
a feeling.
it is a shape
you are being fired into.

paintings.title: ask
paintings.epigraph: “let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach”
paintings.poem:
if you don't know what to do,
ask.

he gives to everyone,
generously,
and never says
you should have known.

but ask like you mean it—
not like a wave
blown one way, then the other,
wanting the answer
and wanting to keep your options open.

paintings.title: wildflower
paintings.epigraph: “like the flower in the grass, he will pass away”
paintings.poem:
the red flowers on the hillside
are beautiful for a week.

then the hot wind comes,
and the sun,
and by noon
they are straw.

so the rich man, too,
in the middle of his busy plans.

the poor brother can lift his head.
he was never counting
on flowers.

paintings.title: no shifting shadow
paintings.epigraph: “Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights”
paintings.poem:
the sun moves,
and the shadow on the sundial
moves with it.

morning, noon, evening—
every light we know
turns.

but the Father of lights
casts no shifting shadow.

every good thing in your hands this morning—
the bread, the breath, the friend—
came down from a hand
that does not change its mind.

paintings.title: the mirror
paintings.epigraph: “he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror”
paintings.poem:
you glance in the bronze mirror,
see the smudge on your cheek,
and walk out the door
without wiping it.

that is hearing
without doing.

the word is not a mirror
to admire.
it is a basin of water
set beside it.

paintings.title: a knock on the door
paintings.epigraph: “to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction”
paintings.poem:
he boils religion down
to a knock on a door.

the widow no one visits.
the child no one claims.

bring bread.
sit a while.
come back next week.

and keep your own hands clean
on the way there.

paintings.title: the good seat
paintings.epigraph: “Sit here in a good place”
paintings.poem:
a gold ring walks in,
and someone jumps up:
here, sit here.

a man in dirty clothes walks in:
you can stand.
or the floor is fine.

we do it without thinking.
James says:
think.

the King you worship
was laid in a feeding trough
and never once
asked for the good seat.

paintings.title: rich
paintings.epigraph: “Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith”
paintings.poem:
look again at the poor man
you asked to stand.

God may have chosen him
first.

heir to a kingdom.
rich
in the only coin
that spends in heaven.

paintings.title: mercy wins
paintings.epigraph: “Mercy triumphs over judgment.”
paintings.poem:
you will be judged
by the same measure
you used on others,

so use a generous one.

in the courtroom of God,
mercy has the last word.
it always
wins the case.

paintings.title: be warmed and filled
paintings.epigraph: “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled”
paintings.poem:
go in peace, we say.
stay warm.
eat well.

and close the door.

a blessing with no bread in it
is just weather.

faith that feeds no one
is a body
with no breath.

paintings.title: they shudder
paintings.epigraph: “The demons also believe, and shudder.”
paintings.poem:
you believe God is one?
good.

so do the demons,
and they shudder.

believing the right facts
is where faith starts,
not where it lives.

faith lives
in what you do
on an ordinary Tuesday.

paintings.title: friend of God
paintings.epigraph: “he was called the friend of God”
paintings.poem:
Abraham believed God,
and it was counted to him
as righteousness.

then he got up
and walked it out—
tent to tent,
year after year,
all the way to the mountain.

that is why they called him
not the believer,
not the scholar,
but the friend of God.

paintings.title: we all stumble
paintings.epigraph: “For we all stumble in many things.”
paintings.poem:
we all stumble,
says the teacher,
putting himself in the we.

that's the first lesson
before you teach:

you are not above the path.
you are on it,
with a scraped knee
like everyone else.

paintings.title: small things steer
paintings.epigraph: “guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires”
paintings.poem:
a bit of iron
turns a horse.
a slab of wood
turns a ship in the wind.

small things steer.

and the smallest steering thing you own
is behind your teeth.

where is it
taking you?

paintings.title: one spark
paintings.epigraph: “See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!”
paintings.poem:
one spark in dry brush.
by evening,
the whole hillside.

one sentence
said in a hot moment,
and a friendship,
a family,
a church,
is smoke.

words are small.
so is an ember.

paintings.title: no one can tame it
paintings.epigraph: “Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing.”
paintings.poem:
we have tamed
beasts and birds,
creatures of the sea.

but no one
has tamed the tongue.

one morning it sings to God.
by afternoon it cuts down
someone made
in his image.

these things,
my brothers,
ought not to be so.

paintings.title: the spring
paintings.epigraph: “Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?”
paintings.poem:
a spring gives one kind of water.
a fig tree gives figs.
a vine doesn't wake up
and try olives.

what comes out of you
tells what is in you.

so don't just watch your words.
ask God
to change the water
at the source.

paintings.title: sown in peace
paintings.epigraph: “the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.”
paintings.poem:
there is a kind of smart
that climbs over people.

and there is wisdom from above:
peaceable. gentle.
willing to listen.
full of mercy.
without a mask.

it doesn't win arguments.
it plants.
and what it plants in peace
comes up
as righteousness.

paintings.title: open hands
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou don’t have, because you don’t ask.”
paintings.poem:
where do the fights come from?
from wanting,
and wanting,
and not having.

we grab.
we scheme.
we elbow.

and never once
simply ask.

and when we do,
it's for more
to spend on ourselves.

open hands, James says.
open to him first.

paintings.title: more grace
paintings.epigraph: “But he gives more grace.”
paintings.poem:
he gives more grace.

three words
for every time
you thought you'd used it up.

and it runs the way water does—
downhill,
to the lowest place.

God resists the proud.
the humble
get flooded.

paintings.title: come close
paintings.epigraph: “Cleanse your hands, you sinners.”
paintings.poem:
come close to God,
and he comes close to you.

it's not a long road.
it's a turn of the body,
a step,
a basin of water,
washed hands,
a heart made single again.

he was always
nearer
than your running.

paintings.title: the chair
paintings.epigraph: “But who are you to judge another?”
paintings.poem:
when you speak against your brother,
you climb into a chair
that isn't yours.

there is one lawgiver.
one judge.
one who can save.

get down from the chair.
sit next to your brother
on the floor.

paintings.title: mist
paintings.epigraph: “For you are a vapor that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away.”
paintings.poem:
tomorrow we'll go to the city,
spend a year,
make a profit—

and the morning mist
lifts off the valley
while we're still talking.

you are mist.
beautiful, brief,
already rising.

so say it the humble way:
if the Lord wills,
we will live,
and do this or that.

paintings.title: the good you know
paintings.epigraph: “To him therefore who knows to do good, and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.”
paintings.poem:
not the wrong you did.
the good you knew
and walked past.

the visit you didn't make.
the gate you didn't mend.
the name you didn't pray.

James counts those too.

and grace
counts them first,
then hands you the hammer.

paintings.title: moth-eaten
paintings.epigraph: “your garments are moth-eaten”
paintings.poem:
the fine robe folded in the chest
for a day that never came.
the moths found it first.

and in the field
the reapers you never paid
are crying out—

and heaven, James says,
has ears.

what you hoard
rots.
what you withhold
testifies.

paintings.title: the farmer
paintings.epigraph: “Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.”
paintings.poem:
the farmer can't hurry the barley.
he plants,
and then he waits
for the autumn rain,
and waits
for the spring rain.

he doesn't dig up the seed
to check on it.

be like that.
steady your heart.
what God has planted
is coming up
on God's time.

paintings.title: the end of the story
paintings.epigraph: “the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.”
paintings.poem:
you've heard of Job:
the ashes, the losses,
the long argument with heaven.

and you've seen the end of the story,
what the Lord did at the last.

endurance is not
pretending it doesn't hurt.
it is still being there
at the end,
where he is full
of compassion
and mercy.

paintings.title: pray, sing
paintings.epigraph: “Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.”
paintings.poem:
is anyone hurting? pray.
is anyone happy? sing.
is anyone sick?
call the elders.
bring the oil.

confess to each other.
pray for each other.

this is how
the first churches
carried each other:
honesty,
oil,
and one another.

paintings.title: like us
paintings.epigraph: “Elijah was a man with a nature like ours”
paintings.poem:
Elijah was just like us,
James says—
same fears,
same moods,
same kind of knees.

and he prayed,
and the sky shut.
and he prayed again,
and the rain came,
and the ground turned green.

don't wait to become a giant
before you pray.
the giants
were ordinary people
who asked.

paintings.title: bring them home
paintings.epigraph: “he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death”
paintings.poem:
and the letter ends
not with a blessing
but with a search party.

if someone wanders,
go after them.

bring them home,
and love
covers a multitude of sins
the way a coat covers
a cold child
on the long walk back.
